Gray * ''Ammanthus'' Boiss. & Heldr. ex Boiss. }} '''''Anthemis''''' is a [[genus]] of aromatic flowering plants in the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Asteraceae]], closely related to ''[[Chamaemelum]]'', and like that genus, known by the common name '''[[chamomile]]'''; some species are also called '''dog-fennel''' or '''mayweed'''. ''Anthemis'' are native to the [[Mediterranean region]] and southwest [[Asia]] east to [[Iran]]. A number of species have also become naturalized in the [[United Kingdom]] and other parts of the world.[http://luirig.altervista.org/flora/taxa/floraspecie.php?genere=Anthemis Altervista Flora Italiana, genere ''Anthemis''] includes photos and European distribution maps[https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/358914#page/335/mode/1up Linnaeus, Carl von. 1753. Species Plantarum 2: 893-896] in Latin[http://www.tropicos.org/Name/40016051 Tropicos, Anthemis L.][http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=102004 Flora of North America ''Anthemis'' Linnaeus] There are around 100 species within this genus.{{Cite web|title=How to Propagate and Grow Anthemis ?|url=https://www.floristlondon.co.uk/how-to-propagate-and-grow-anthemis|access-date=2020-08-08|website=Florist London|language=en-GB}} ''Anthemis'' species are used as food plants by the [[larva]]e of some [[Lepidoptera]] species including ''[[Orthonama obstipata]]'' (The Gem) and ''[[Bucculatrix anthemidella]]'', a leaf-miner which feeds exclusively on ''Anthemis tinctoria''. ==Cultivation and uses== Several species and [[cultivar]]s are available for garden use.
